entities.summary:
François-Marie, 1st duc de Broglie (1671–1745), emerged as a pivotal military commander and diplomat during the waning years of Louis XIV's reign and the subsequent regency and reign of Louis XV. A scion of the Piedmontese House of Broglia, which had relocated to France, he distinguished himself through a career spanning nearly five decades, marked by service in major European conflicts from the War of the Spanish Succession to the War of the Austrian Succession. His strategic acumen and political astuteness positioned him as a key figure in the French military establishment, contributing significantly to France's geopolitical standing in Western Europe during a period of intense dynastic rivalries and shifting alliances.

Broglie's military career began in earnest during the War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714), where he fought with distinction in numerous campaigns, earning promotion to Maréchal de camp by 1710. His service continued through the War of the Polish Succession (1733–1738), where he commanded French forces in Italy, notably leading the French to victory at the Battle of Crocetta in 1734. Elevated to Maréchal de France in 1734, he subsequently assumed command of the Army of Bohemia during the early stages of the War of the Austrian Succession (1740–1748), navigating complex logistical challenges and political pressures in Central Europe. Beyond his martial exploits, Broglie served as Governor of Strasbourg (1724–1728) and Languedoc (1728–1745), demonstrating administrative capability and securing his family's influence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: François-Marie de Broglie was a prominent French military commander whose service in three major European wars shaped French strategic interests and solidified the Broglie family's aristocratic influence for generations. His career demonstrates the critical role of noble military leadership in maintaining France's power balance in the 18th century.
